title: Permission denied
summary: Diagnose a service that cannot read its configuration and fix file modes with least access.

scenario.briefing: The orders API cannot read its configuration. A secret key is also world-readable. Repair both permissions with the least access needed, then restart and verify the service.

objectives.description: Make the config readable by its owner and group only.
Limit the API key to its owner.
Restart the service and verify it runs.
Check understanding through the remaining explanation and transfer evidence.

hints: Run systemctl status orders-api and journalctl -u orders-api.
List details with ls -l. The config currently has mode 000.
Use chmod 640 for config.json and chmod 600 for api.key.
journalctl -u orders-api; ls -l app secrets; chmod 640 app/config.json; chmod 600 secrets/api.key; systemctl restart orders-api.

misconceptions.description: Granting everyone access to fix a permission error.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Sets config.json or api.key to mode 777 instead of the least access required.
misconceptions.feedback: World-writable configuration and secrets are a security failure. Grant only the access the service needs.

misconceptions.description: Leaving a secret readable by every user.
misconceptions.feedback: Secret material should not be world-readable. Mode 600 limits read and write to the owner.

misconceptions.description: Believing mode 777 is an acceptable fix for configuration errors.
misconceptions.feedback: Broad access solves today's error and creates a security problem. Use the narrowest mode that lets the service work.

sections.title: Permissions answer who can do what
sections.body: Unix file modes describe read, write, and execute access for the owner, group, and others. A service runs as a user and needs just enough access to read its files. Permission errors are diagnosed by checking both the running user and the mode.

sections.title: Least privilege
sections.body: Making a file world-readable may stop an error, but it also exposes data. Secrets such as API keys should be readable only by the account that needs them. Configuration is usually readable by the service user and its group.

vocabulary.definition: A numeric description of read, write, and execute permissions.
The user account that owns a file.
Granting only the access required for a task.

hints: Diagnose the permission error, set the config and key modes, restart, and verify.
File modes grant read, write, and execute separately to owner, group, and others.
Mode 640 lets the owner read and write and the group read, while others get nothing.
Set config.json to 640 and secrets/api.key to 600, restart orders-api, then confirm it is running.
steps.title: Repair file access
steps.prompt: Use the terminal. Diagnose the failure, set config.json to 640, set secrets/api.key to 600, restart orders-api, and verify it runs.
steps.explanation: The service could not read a config with no permissions. Modes 640 and 600 grant necessary access without exposing secrets, and the restarted service is running.

hints: Select statements about least access and how permissions are evaluated.
Permissions apply to the user the service runs as; secrets need narrower access than config.
A shared team file can be 640, while a private key should be 600.
Three statements are accurate; reject mode 777 as a fix.
steps.title: Least access

statements.label: Permissions depend on the user the service runs as.
Mode 777 is an acceptable fix for configuration errors.
Secret files should be readable only by the accounts that need them.
The service log can identify a permission failure.

steps.explanation: Permissions are evaluated for a specific user. Broad access solves today's error and creates a security problem.

accessibility.summary: The terminal is keyboard-first and objectives are text. File listings include textual permission descriptions.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Type commands and press Enter. The output log scrolls with arrow keys.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: ls -l output is announced as mode, owner, group, size, and path. Permission changes are confirmed in text.
